title: Core: repartitioning data files written with an old partition spec
summary: mukund-thakur proposed support for rewriting only the data files that belong to an old partition spec so they conform to the current spec (PR #16190). Today such files are skipped by rewrite jobs when they already have the target size. Using rewrite-all with a filter and partial progress does not work well for large tables, because a rerun after a failure picks up the same files again and files cannot be filtered by spec ID. He suggested a new rewrite-partition-spec-mismatch flag used together with partial-progress.enabled, and later mentioned an optimized repartitioning algorithm in PR #16515. Imran Rashid, who works with the author, said this matters for large tables because storage-partitioned joins need consistent partitioning and existing tools cannot make incremental progress. pan3793 supported it, having seen SPJ fail because a scan mixed old-spec files. No committer feedback on the design appears in the thread.

positions.stance: Add a rewrite-partition-spec-mismatch option so that rewrite jobs pick up only files written with an old partition spec and can make partial progress.
Large tables need an incremental way to move old data to the new partitioning, in particular because storage-partitioned joins require consistent partitioning.
Supports the change after finding that SPJ did not work because the scan mixed data files not matching the current partition spec.

outcome.note: Two supporting replies; no review of the proposed option or decision appears in the thread.

why_it_matters: Tables whose partition spec has evolved currently have no incremental, restartable way to bring old files to the new spec, which blocks storage-partitioned joins on them.
